title: Directed acyclic graphs to minimise bias and optimise causal inference in SNAP-3: an observational cohort study of frailty, multimorbidity, and delirium in older surgical patients.
authors: Swarbrick CJ, Blake HA, Martin P, Partridge JSL, Moppett IK.

Types of causal pathways and key types of variables on noncausal pathways in a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Simplified example DAGs to demonstrate the concepts and structure of DAGs. DAG, directed acyclic graph.

Directed acyclic graph (DAG) illustrating the relationship between frailty and multimorbidity with morbidity. An example DAG illustrates the exposure–outcome relationship between frailty and multimorbidity (as a joint exposure or interacting exposures) with postoperative (postop) morbidity (outcome) as shown in DAGitty. The joint exposures, frailty and multimorbidity, are represented by green node
